meta.titre: Weathering Profiles and Residual Ores: how laterite, bauxite and nickel ores form
meta.sous_theme: Tropical weathering and residual mineral deposits

sections.contenu_markdown: In the humid tropics, road cuttings often expose red, clay-rich ground many metres deep above weathered rock. This laterite is used for bricks and road fill, and in some places the same weathering has concentrated aluminium or nickel into ores that can be mined. Examiners ask for the zones of a weathering profile, the conditions that favour deep weathering and the way different parent rocks, such as granite and peridotite, give different products. This course gives you the profile, the chemistry and the contrasts you need.

items: Chemical weathering includes hydrolysis, oxidation and solution, and it is fastest in warm, wet climates.
Feldspar weathers to clay minerals such as kaolinite, while quartz resists weathering.
Granite is rich in feldspar and quartz, whereas peridotite is an ultramafic rock made mainly of olivine and pyroxene.
Aluminium and iron form oxides and hydroxides that are very insoluble in natural surface water.

sections.titre: Tropical weathering profiles and residual ore deposits
sections.contenu_markdown:
### The weathering profile
From the surface downwards, a deep tropical profile has these zones (names vary between books):

| Zone | Description |
|---|---|
| Surface cap | A hard crust of aluminium hydroxides (bauxite) or iron oxides, depending on the parent rock |
| Laterite and clay zone | Red, yellow or mottled clay-rich material from which most soluble elements have gone |
| Saprolite | Deeply weathered rock that is soft but still keeps the original rock texture |
| Partly weathered rock | Hard core blocks (corestones) in a weathered mass, at the weathering front |
| Fresh bedrock | Unweathered parent rock |

### Conditions that favour deep weathering
- Warm, wet climate: reactions are fast and plenty of water leaches the products.
- Good drainage and gentle relief: water percolates and drains away, while erosion is slow enough for the profile to thicken.
- Long time and tectonic stability.
- Vegetation: decay gives organic acids and carbon dioxide, making soil water acidic.
- Suitable parent rock: aluminium-rich rocks such as granite for bauxite, ultramafic rocks such as peridotite for nickel.

### Chemistry of residual enrichment
Hydrolysis changes feldspar to kaolinite and releases soluble ions, for example $2\mathrm{KAlSi_3O_8} + 2\mathrm{H^+} + 9\mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow \mathrm{Al_2Si_2O_5(OH)_4} + 4\mathrm{H_4SiO_4} + 2\mathrm{K^+}$. Intense leaching then removes silica from kaolinite: $\mathrm{Al_2Si_2O_5(OH)_4} + 5\mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Al(OH)_3} + 2\mathrm{H_4SiO_4}$. Sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium and silica are carried away in solution, while aluminium and iron form very insoluble hydroxides and oxides and stay behind. This is **residual enrichment**: the ore forms because the waste is removed. **Bauxite**, rich in gibbsite, is the main ore of aluminium.

### Nickel laterite on peridotite
Weathering of olivine- and pyroxene-rich peridotite removes magnesium and silica, and iron is oxidised to an iron oxide cap. Nickel is released, carried downward in solution and deposited again in the lower altered peridotite, so the ore zone lies below the iron-rich cap and holds more nickel than the fresh rock.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked how an aluminium ore forms or what is found at the top of a profile on granite.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give the sequence: hydrolysis of feldspar to kaolinite, leaching of sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium and silica, and accumulation of aluminium hydroxide (gibbsite) as bauxite at the surface. Add the conditions: warm, wet climate, good drainage, gentle relief, long time.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the parent rock is ultramafic, or a question asks what forms at the top and base of a profile on peridotite.
variantes.contenu_markdown: At the top is an iron oxide cap with little nickel, below it is leached laterite, and the nickel ore lies in the altered peridotite lower down, where nickel from above has been redeposited. The contrast with granite is that the parent rock supplies nickel and magnesium and not aluminium, so the surface product is iron-rich and not bauxite.

variantes.nom: Naming the products at labelled levels
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a profile is described and the products at chosen levels must be named.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Identify the parent rock first. On granite the surface product is bauxite, with the soluble elements removed, deeply weathered rock below and unweathered granite at the base. On peridotite the surface product is an iron oxide cap, with the nickel-rich altered peridotite below. State the product and, where asked, what was removed.

sections.enonce_markdown: Explain how bauxite forms from a granite in a hot, wet region. (8 marks)

etapes.justification: Explain needs a chain of processes, and the starting material and the climate are both given.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Plan: (1) climate and water supply, (2) hydrolysis of feldspar, (3) leaching, (4) concentration of aluminium, (5) conditions needed.

etapes.justification: A hot, wet climate speeds up chemical reactions and supplies water to remove products.
etapes.resultat_markdown: High temperature and heavy rainfall give fast chemical weathering and deep percolation of acidic water.

etapes.justification: Granite is rich in feldspar, so this is the key reaction.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Feldspar reacts with water and hydrogen ions to give kaolinite, and potassium and sodium ions and silica go into solution.

etapes.justification: The ore forms because soluble material is lost, not because aluminium is added.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Continued leaching removes sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium and silica, including silica from kaolinite. Aluminium is insoluble, so it accumulates as gibbsite, a main mineral of bauxite.

etapes.justification: A deep deposit needs the right setting for a long time.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Good drainage and gentle relief remove solutions without stripping the profile, and long tectonic stability allows the layer to thicken.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Model answer.** In a hot, wet climate, chemical weathering is fast and acidic water percolates deeply. Feldspar in the granite is hydrolysed to kaolinite, and sodium, potassium and silica are released into solution. Prolonged leaching removes sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium and silica, even from kaolinite, while aluminium, which is very insoluble, stays behind and accumulates as aluminium hydroxide (gibbsite), the main mineral of bauxite. This is residual enrichment. Good drainage and gentle relief allow the solutions to drain away without the profile being eroded, and long stability lets the layer thicken at the surface.

items.erreur_markdown: Bauxite forms in deserts because evaporation concentrates aluminium.
items.pourquoi_faux: Bauxite needs heavy leaching in a warm, wet climate. A dry climate has too little water to remove the soluble elements.
items.correction_markdown: Write that bauxite forms in warm, wet regions by leaching of soluble elements, leaving aluminium behind.

items.pourquoi_faux: Bauxite is the aluminium-rich kind of laterite. Iron-rich laterite is not an aluminium ore.
items.correction_markdown: Write that bauxite is aluminium-rich and that an iron-rich laterite is a different product.

items.erreur_markdown: Weathering removes aluminium and iron and leaves silica behind.
items.pourquoi_faux: Aluminium and iron oxides and hydroxides are insoluble and remain. Silica and the alkali and alkaline-earth ions are the ones leached out.
items.correction_markdown: Write that Na, K, Ca, Mg and silica are removed, whereas Al and Fe stay as residual oxides.

items.pourquoi_faux: The nickel comes from ultramafic rock such as peridotite. Granite contains very little nickel.
items.correction_markdown: Write that nickel laterite forms on ultramafic parent rock.

items.pourquoi_faux: Saprolite is deeply weathered, soft rock that keeps the original rock texture. Fresh bedrock is the unweathered base of the profile.
items.correction_markdown: Describe saprolite as weathered rock that still shows the original fabric.

items.enonce_markdown: Arrange these zones of a profile on granite in order from the surface downwards: fresh granite, saprolite, bauxite cap, partly weathered rock with corestones. Name two elements removed in solution and one element that stays behind.
items.solution_markdown: **Bauxite cap, saprolite, partly weathered rock with corestones, fresh granite.** Removed in solution (any two): sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium; silica is also lost. Residual: **aluminium** (iron also stays). Award a mark for the order and a mark for each correct statement about removal and residue.

items.enonce_markdown: A granite contains 14% aluminium oxide. The bauxite formed from it contains 56% aluminium oxide. Assume that the aluminium oxide did not move. (a) By what factor was the aluminium oxide concentrated? (b) What fraction of the original mass was lost? (c) Why is the assumption only approximate?
items.solution_markdown: (a) Factor $= \dfrac{56}{14} = $ **4**. (b) Fraction lost $= 1 - \dfrac{14}{56} = $ **0.75**, that is 75% of the original mass. (c) Acidic, organic-rich water can dissolve and move some aluminium, so part of it is lost or redeposited. Award a mark for each result and for the reason.

items.enonce_markdown: A fresh peridotite contains 0.3% nickel, and the enriched zone of its weathering profile contains 2.4%. (a) Calculate the enrichment factor. (b) Compare how nickel laterite on peridotite and bauxite on granite form, in terms of parent rock and the behaviour of the metal. (c) Explain why a dry climate with very little rain is unfavourable for both.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Factor $= \dfrac{2.4}{0.3} = $ **8**. (b) Both are residual deposits made by leaching. For bauxite the parent rock is aluminium-rich (granite) and aluminium is insoluble, so it stays near the surface. For nickel laterite the parent rock is ultramafic (peridotite); magnesium and silica are leached, iron stays as an oxide cap, and nickel is partly dissolved, carried down and redeposited in the altered peridotite below, so the ore lies lower in the profile. (c) With little rain there is not enough water to dissolve and remove the soluble elements, and weathering is slow, so deep profiles and residual enrichment do not develop. Award marks for the factor, for the parent rock of each ore, for the behaviour of each metal and for the climate reason.

items_markdown: A deep tropical profile runs from a surface cap through a laterite and clay zone and saprolite to partly weathered rock and fresh bedrock.
Deep weathering needs a warm, wet climate, good drainage, gentle relief, long stability and a suitable parent rock.
Residual enrichment: soluble elements (Na, K, Ca, Mg, silica) are leached away, while insoluble aluminium and iron stay behind.
Granite gives bauxite at the surface; peridotite gives an iron oxide cap with nickel ore lower in the altered rock.
Bauxite, rich in gibbsite, is the main ore of aluminium; laterite is also used for bricks and road fill.
